item.title: Owara Kaze no Bon: A Haunting Lantern-Lit Dance Festival in Yatsuo — Guide
item.description: Owara Kaze no Bon is a centuries-old festival held each September in the hillside town of Yatsuo, originally performed as a ritual to ward off the autumn winds that threatened the year’s rice harvest. Dancers, often wearing straw hats that partially obscure their faces or delicate masks, perform slow, elegant, flowing movements through the town’s lantern-lit streets late into the night, accompanied by melancholic shamisen and kokyu string music that gives the festival its distinctively haunting, wistful atmosphere.

item.title: Toyama Hidden Gems: Yatsuo's Ghost Festival, Inami's 1700 Woodcarvers & Tonami's Tulip Fields
item.description: Toyama’s best-known attractions — the Alpine Route, Gokayama, the Kurobe Gorge — draw most visitors and most travel writing. What lies around them is a constellation of experiences that receive a fraction of the attention: a dance festival considered Japan’s most hauntingly beautiful, a town where woodcarving is still a living trade practised by 1,700 artisans, and a volcanic caldera most Alpine Route visitors pass directly over without knowing it exists.
